scenes.line1: Can Go structs act like objects?
scenes.say: Can Go structs act like objects? What makes methods on structs so important in interviews?

scenes.label: Structs
scenes.sub: Group related fields together in Go.
scenes.say: Structs in Go group related fields together. They're the building blocks for custom data types.
You can define methods on structs. Use a value receiver for GetName, and a pointer receiver for SetName to actually change the Name field.
Value receivers work on a copy of the struct, so changes don't stick. Pointer receivers work on the original, letting you modify its fields.

scenes.question: When should you use a pointer receiver?
scenes.right: Use pointer receivers to modify data or avoid copying big structs.
scenes.say: Interview trap: When should you use a pointer receiver? It's not always. Use them when you need to change the struct or avoid copying large data.
